banner: Post-call version. Sources: 8-K exhibits 99.1 (release) and 99.2 (presentation) and the 3Q26 10-Q, all filed 12 November 2026; call transcript of 12 November (Motley Fool); 2Q26 call summary (Nasdaq). Four quarters of public history (IPO October 2025); full Q&A held for 3Q26 only.
changes: TensorWave lease terminated on 10 November after its closing date passed (10-Q); AMD credit support falls away with it.

Replacement is a non-binding LOI with an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler for about 600 MW of powered land, plus a $200mn prepayment agreement (wire due 13 November per the call) and a $15mn early-works agreement; a $90mn steel purchase is still being finalized.

Model pivot to 'Powered Land Plus': the customer builds its own data halls, so Fermi's capex per MW falls to the company's cited $3.9-5.1mn benchmark, and so does rent (benchmark $55-69 per kW-month).

10-Q: resources 'not sufficient' for 12 months before management plans; substantial doubt judged alleviated only by capex sequencing, undrawn equipment facilities and possible asset sales. The turbine warehouse lenders (MUFG assigned the loan to a new syndicate on 9 October) require committed project financing for 400 MW by 10 February 2027 or it is an event of default.
First power restated as late 2Q or early 3Q27 for the first building (2Q call: 210 MW on 1 July 2027); on-site mobilization targeted for 1 December.

All core figures confirmed. Unverified or single source: 2Q PP&E additions 185.0 (press, not stated in the 2Q 10-Q, which gives 1H 626.2); TensorWave 222 MW (prior Field Guide records, not in the 3Q 10-Q); broker Buy ratings in the consensus card (carried from the preview); founder sale demand (Stocktwits, 9 November). Price $2.05 on 12 November (BigGo, single source); today's price not checked. The $200mn wire was due 13 November; receipt not confirmed at writing.
consensus_thesis: Brokers rate Fermi a Buy as an option on scarce Texas power assets and a signed TensorWave lease; at about $1.8 before results the stock priced distress or heavy dilution (Provisional, from the 12 November preview).
headline: The call made the hyperscaler deal more concrete ($200mn wire due 13 November, site mobilization 1 December) but the 10-Q shows it is a non-binding letter of intent racing three hard deadlines (Texas Tech and Keystone on 31 December, turbine-loan project financing on 10 February 2027); the thesis is now binary on a signed lease, and credit quality stays weak until one exists.
kona: Fermi's pivot shows where the bankable middle is for a behind-the-meter campus: sell powered land to an investment-grade tenant that builds its own halls, take a prepayment to bridge, and keep capex near $4-5mn per MW. But a non-binding LOI did not satisfy Fermi's lenders or landlord, so Kona should avoid loan or land milestones tied to a lease date it does not control, and should treat a prepayment as bridge money, with its refund terms negotiated before first draw.
monitor: Receipt of the $200mn wire (due 13 November) and whether it is refundable if no lease is signed.
Definitive lease by 31 December: it is the condition for the Texas Tech notice to proceed and the Keystone approved-customer test.
A fully committed project financing for 400 MW by 10 February 2027 (event-of-default trigger on the $445mn turbine warehouse loan, ex-MUFG).
name: Fermi America

sections.body: Emphasized more: investment-grade hyperscalers only, 'safe harbor' sites as ERCOT freezes large loads, Powered Land Plus economics, Texas Tech support. Less or dropped: TensorWave and neocloud tenants; turnkey builds; Hillcore (not mentioned on the call; still in the 10-Q); a dated MW figure for first power. KPIs more important: cash receipts, lease signing date, project-financing commitments. Risks up: covenant deadlines, single-tenant dependence. Down: tenant credit quality, Fermi capex per MW. → Fermi has traded a larger revenue line for a smaller capital need; that is the right trade if it signs, because lenders will lend against an investment-grade lease at a fraction of today's 12-13%.

sections.body: $mn. Gap = PP&E additions plus operating burn (our calc), before equipment-facility draws. Next dollar: secured equipment debt at 12.0-12.9% fixed or SOFR+4% (turbine warehouse, ex-MUFG; the 9 October amendment removed the 10 November lease trigger for $25mn of fees); the 5% convert traded at ~83.5% of par on 30 September. Maturities in 24 months: turbine warehouse loan $444.9mn (10 August 2027). Remaining 2026 purchase commitments $22.0mn. Market cap ~$1.32bn at $2.05 on 12 November (BigGo Finance, single source) vs net PP&E $1.67bn. Illustrative only, using the company's market benchmarks, not Fermi terms: 600 MW at $55-69 per kW-month is $396-497mn a year of fixed charges against $2.3-3.1bn of PLP build cost, a 13-21% gross yield (our calc). → A signed IG lease would let Fermi borrow far below 12%; without it, the next dollar is equity near $2.

head: Question for owners
Why it matters
Asked on call?
rows: The 10-Q calls the hyperscaler deal a non-binding LOI. If no lease is signed, must the $200mn be repaid, and is it secured ahead of the converts?
Wire date asked (13 Nov); refund terms not asked
The turbine warehouse lenders (ex-MUFG) need committed financing for 400 MW of generation by 10 February 2027. Who is providing it, and does a lease signed in December leave time to close it?
Texas Tech's notice to proceed requires a signed 200 MW Phase 1 lease by 31 December. Will the lease be signed by then, or is an extension agreed?
You cite $55-69 per kW-month for powered land. Will Fermi's fixed charges sit inside that range, above it for behind-the-meter power, or below it?
The 10-Q says cash is not sufficient for 12 months before management plans. Without the prepayment, how many months of runway, and is an equity raise planned?
Is the board running a sale process in parallel, as the largest shareholder demands?
